title: AiEvidenceEnvelopeV2
description: Tamper-evident evidence envelope for an AI generation call, version 2. The envelope is the metadata document of a JAdES-sealed evidence record (ETSI TS 119 182-1): it is canonicalized (RFC 8785 / JCS) and signed as detached object 0 of a multi-object sigD (ObjectIdByURIHash), alongside the content payloads it describes. Unlike v1 it carries no integrity or proof fields of its own — hashing, timestamping and origin are owned entirely by the enclosing JAdES signature. Content payloads are referenced by URI only; their digests live in the signed sigD.hashV, never in the envelope. See ai-evidence-envelope-v2.md for the normative specification.

schemaName.description: Stable schema identifier. Always 'AiEvidenceEnvelope' for this family.

schemaVersion.description: Major version of the envelope schema. Breaking changes increment this.

evidenceId.description: Stable identifier for this evidence record. Generated by the producer; never reused.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp the envelope was assembled. Distinct from the signature's iat claim and from any sigTst genTime.

category.description: Free-form classifier for why the AI call was made (e.g. 'classification', 'summarization', 'advisory').

type.description: Whether the call was driven by a human user, a backend service, an autonomous system, or an AI agent acting with delegated autonomy. 'agent' is new in v2.

id.description: Stable identifier for the actor (e.g. user UUID, service principal, workload identity). NOT the actor's name or PII. SDKs offer hashing this value at source; see spec §9.

tenantId.description: Optional tenant the actor belongs to.

displayHint.description: Optional non-PII display hint (e.g. role, department).

correlationId.description: Tracing/correlation id linking this evidence to the parent business transaction.

parentEvidenceId.description: Optional semantic link to a prior envelope this one continues from. Distinct from 'chain', which is a cryptographic sequence; see spec §5.4.

name.description: Model identifier as reported by the provider (e.g. 'claude-fable-5').

version.description: Provider-reported model version or build, if any.

deploymentId.description: Optional deployment-specific identifier (e.g. Azure deployment name).

parameters.description: Sampling parameters used (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, ...). Recorded verbatim.

objects.description: Descriptive list of the detached content payloads this evidence references, index-aligned with sigD.pars[1..n] of the enclosing JAdES signature (the envelope itself is pars[0] and is NOT listed here). URIs MUST be unique across the array (byte-exact string comparison) and MUST NOT equal the reserved envelope URI 'urn:sigill:envelope'. The envelope says what each object IS; the signature says what it HASHES TO. An empty array is a metadata-only record. Digests are deliberately absent here — the one and only copy of each content hash is the signed copy in sigD.hashV.

uri.description: Caller-chosen identifier for the payload ('urn:...' recommended; filenames and storage keys accepted). Opaque to Sigill; never dereferenced. MUST match the corresponding sigD.pars entry byte-exactly.

role.description: What the payload is: the prompt, a structured input (tool/function arguments, attachments), retrieved context (RAG), the model's primary output, a generated artifact beyond the primary output, or an execution log.

contentType.description: MIME type of the payload (e.g. 'text/plain', 'application/json'). When present it MUST match the corresponding sigD.ctys entry byte-exactly; when absent the ctys entry is the empty string.

encoding.description: How the payload bytes that were hashed were derived: 'utf-8' for text serialized as UTF-8, 'binary' for raw file bytes. RECOMMENDED for text payloads — without it a verifier handed a string cannot reliably reproduce the digest. (v1's 'base64' value is removed together with inline payloads.)

sizeBytes.description: Optional: size of the payload bytes that were hashed.

metadata.description: Optional structured metadata about the payload. Well-known keys (all optional, typed below) cover RAG retrieval attributes carried by v1's retrievedContext entries; additional keys are producer-defined.

source.description: Source document identifier or URI, for role 'context'.

language.description: BCP 47 language tag of the payload, if known.

sourceTrace.description: Provenance trail: where did the retrieved context originate? Useful for downstream auditability. Unchanged from v1.

policyMetadata.description: Applied policies, redactions, and content filters at the time of the call.

redactionPolicy.description: Identifier of the redaction policy applied (e.g. 'pii-redaction-v3').

chain.description: RESERVED (mechanism defined, semantics deliberately open in v2.0): cryptographic sequencing for multi-step agent runs. What constitutes a 'step' (turn / tool call / run) is out of scope for v2.0. See spec §5.4.

seq.description: Zero-based position of this envelope in the run's chain.

prevSignatureSha256.description: Lowercase SHA-256 hex over the previous step's signature. RECOMMENDED preimage: the base64url-decoded JWS Signature Value of the previous artifact's classical signature; the exact preimage is among the open v2.0 semantics. Absent for the first step (seq 0).

extensions.description: Named extension point for profile- or producer-specific data that is not part of the shared envelope-family core. Each key is an extension identifier (a registered profile name such as 'sigill-evidence', or reverse-DNS for producer-private extensions); each value is an object owned entirely by that extension. Extensions are signed like everything else in the envelope but carry no cross-profile semantics; generic viewers and verifiers ignore extensions they do not know.

contentHash.description: A standalone digest, used only where a hash is data ABOUT something (e.g. sourceTrace.snapshotHash) — never for binding the evidence payloads, which is sigD's job.

sizeBytes.description: Optional: size of the input bytes that were hashed.
